root_cause_criterion.description: After copying upwd via strncpy, len must still equal the caller-supplied buffer size. The vulnerable code assigns strncpy's char* return to size_t len, corrupting it from the actual buffer size to a stack pointer value.

nodes.description: memcmp(old_hmac, new_hmac, shasize) reads 20 bytes starting at old_hmac (buf+24). With a 28-byte buffer, the last 16 bytes extend into uninitialized heap memory, triggering MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.

edges.description: The corrupted len (stack pointer value instead of actual buffer size) is passed to stun_attr_get_first_by_type_str, where stun_get_command_message_len_str's check bufLen > len vacuously passes because bufLen (44) is less than the corrupted len (~0x7fff...).

The sar reference found through the bounds-bypassed attribute search is passed to stun_attr_get_value, which extracts old_hmac pointing to buf+24 — 4 bytes before the 28-byte buffer ends, while the declared attribute length is 20.
